## Constants

<a name="configurationWidth"></a>Layout of the configuration display, in terminal columns.

- configurationWidth: the width of the whole display
- configurationLabelWidth: the width of the label column, including the gap after a label
- configurationColumnGap: the least space between a label and its value

```go
const (
    configurationWidth      = 60
    configurationLabelWidth = 18
    configurationColumnGap  = 2
)
```

<a name="displayValue"></a>
## func displayValue

```go
func displayValue(value any) string
```

displayValue returns the text of a string, integer, or list value, with a list in brackets. It returns the unset marker for a nil pointer, a nil list, and an empty string.

<a name="formatConfigurationField"></a>
## func formatConfigurationField

```go
func formatConfigurationField(fieldLabel string, configuredValue any) string
```

formatConfigurationField returns the terminal output for one setting: the label in a fixed\-width column with the value beside it, each wrapped onto further lines as needed. A list value is joined with commas, an unset value shows the unset marker, and an empty value shows the empty marker.

<a name="render"></a>
## func render

```go
func render(writer io.Writer, asJSON bool, command string, result saferm.Result) error
```

render writes an operation's result to the writer, either as JSON or through the plain\-text template that fits the command and the contents of the result.

<a name="renderJSON"></a>
## func renderJSON

```go
func renderJSON(writer io.Writer, command string, result saferm.Result) error
```

renderJSON writes the result as JSON:

- the settings, for a result that has settings and no notice
- the list of actions, for the list command
- the action, for the view command

For every other command it writes the whole result. A delete, move, dispose, restore, or purge result holds its actions in a list, also when it holds one action, with any problems beside them.

renderTemplate executes the named result template with the data and writes the output to the writer with its tab\-separated columns aligned.

<a name="Terminal"></a>
## type Terminal

Terminal carries out a request on the streams of one invocation.

- Input: the source of confirmation answers
- Output: the destination for results
- Errors: the destination for failures and confirmation prompts
- JSON: whether to write JSON instead of plain text

```go
type Terminal struct {
    Input  io.Reader
    Output io.Writer
    Errors io.Writer
    JSON   bool
}
```

<a name="Terminal.Execute"></a>
### func \(Terminal\) Execute

```go
func (terminal Terminal) Execute(ctx context.Context, request *saferm.Request) error
```

Execute carries out the request through saferm.Run and writes its result. When the operation needs confirmation, Execute prompts for it, then either reruns the request as confirmed or writes a cancellation notice. It writes a result that accompanies an error and returns that error.

<a name="Terminal.Failure"></a>
### func \(Terminal\) Failure

```go
func (terminal Terminal) Failure(err error) error
```

Failure writes the error to the Errors stream, as a JSON object when JSON is set.

<a name="Terminal.confirm"></a>
### func \(Terminal\) confirm

```go
func (terminal Terminal) confirm(ctx context.Context, confirmation saferm.Confirmation) (bool, error)
```

confirm writes the confirmation's prompt to the Errors stream, reads one line from Input, and reports whether that line confirms. The line confirms when it is y or yes in any letter case, or when it is empty and the confirmation defaults to yes. Input that ends before a full line does not confirm.

<a name="answer"></a>
## type answer

answer is one line read from the confirmation input, with the error that ended the read, if any.

```go
type answer struct {
    text string
    err  error
}
```
